html:
SMTO-LLM-0068 — SMTO couldn't get an answer from the local model server

GUID: 22470790-7c7f-50fc-9a7d-a998a5ae88c0
Slug: local-ai-health-failed
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO asked the model server on the Gateway computer whether it was working, but got no usable answer in time. This was only a check; nothing was started, stopped or downloaded.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In a new message, ask SMTO to show the status of the local AI model servers on that Gateway and whether the one you use is running. If the model server has stopped or is still starting up, the check fails even though the settings are correct.
  2. Open Parameter Store, find the Local AI Runtime profile you used, and confirm its host and port match where the model server actually listens. A wrong port or address sends the check to a place where no model server is answering.
  3. If the model server needs an API key, confirm the profile's linked Local AI API key entry holds the current key. A missing or old key makes the model server refuse the check.
  4. If the server is busy loading a large model, wait a minute, then ask SMTO to check the model server's health again. A server that is still loading may not answer within the few seconds the check allows.

What success looks like

  • When you ask SMTO to check that model server, it reports the server as ready and lists its models.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't stop or kill a model server that SMTO didn't start; someone else may be using it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Local AI read request (health, models, metrics or status) to the profile's endpoint failed, returned a non-success status, exceeded its read deadline or raised an unexpected read-side error, so readiness was not established.

What this means

  • A bounded health/read request failed, exceeded its read deadline or raised an unclassified read-side exception; readiness has not been established. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • A bounded health/read request failed, exceeded its read deadline or raised an unclassified read-side exception; readiness has not been established.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact runtime state, endpoint HTTP status and health timeout; inspect authentication and response format without exposing credentials.

How to fix it

  • On the profile's Gateway, confirm the provider is listening on the profile's host and port and that its health/models path (for example /health, /api/version or the API root's /models) answers within health_timeout (1-10 s, default 3) with the accepted API key. Check the accepted Local AI Runtime profile in Parameter Store for a wrong host, port, API root or api_key_ref; do not stop a process the Gateway does not own to make the check pass.
  • Repair the identified endpoint, access or readiness issue; keep existing runtime ownership and inspect mutation receipts separately.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended endpoint passes its supported bounded health check.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
